messages:
Alex Chen (Support): Customer 'Northgate Retail' reporting sudden p95/p99 regression on tool-heavy flows starting 07:12 UTC after router rollout. Their p95 jumped from ~200ms to ~420ms, p99 from 900ms to ~2.6s. No increase in 5xx, but a lot more client-side timeouts. Ticket: SUP-4521. tagging @Maria and @Samir.
Maria Gomez (SRE): Confirmed region eu-central-1 spike 07:10-07:25. Traces show long tail inside 'tool_router' and 'schema_validator' spans. Heatmap shows frequent 150-400ms per-request router overhead for sessions that use >2 tools.
Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): The router v2 change moved JSON schema validation to a synchronous pre-check for structured outputs. That makes the router do extra CPU work before routing to tools. We intended async validation but merged the wrong flag.
Alex Chen (Support): Customer says they call 4 tools in their flow (extract->classify->normalize->persist). Each tool call is small but router overhead compounds. Can reproduce?
Alex Chen (Support): Repro steps provided by customer (sanitized):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"process batch invoices"}],"tools":["extractor","classifier","normalizer","db_writer"]}'

Priya Rao (DevEx): Did we enable strict JSON schema mode? Any new validators shipped? Also are we doing schema compile per-request? That would kill latency.
Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): Yep, STRICT_SCHEMA=true in router config and we compile schema on first validate then cache, but compilation still runs when schema changes. However, we also run validation on the request path synchronously which adds 40-220ms depending on output complexity.
JenkinsBot: DEPLOYMENT: router-v2 config update applied to eu-central-1 at 07:05 UTC
Maria Gomez (SRE): Immediate mitigations we can perform:
- Pin impacted customers to router-v1 (routing rule)
- Roll back the STRICT_SCHEMA=true flag or flip to ASYNC_VALIDATE=true
- Add short-circuit header x-redwood-skip-validate for critical customers (support opt-in)
- Increase router concurrency and tune thread pool sharing

Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): Short-term: I'll flip ASYNC_VALIDATE=true in config and push a canary for 10% traffic, that should reduce per-request router time. Medium-term: change code path so validation runs post-tool and off the critical path, or run validation in a validation worker pool.
Alex Chen (Support): Customer asked for ETA. What do we think for canary flip?
Maria Gomez (SRE): Canary config flip now, monitoring.
OpsBot: CANARY CONFIG CHANGE: ASYNC_VALIDATE=true deployed to 10% in eu-central-1
Alex Chen (Support): Running repro locally with strict vs async:
```
# strict (sync validation)
p95: 430ms
p99: 2.5s
# async_validation
p95: 210ms
p99: 780ms
```
Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): Numbers look right. Async reduces tail significantly. For customers that need strict structured output correctness we should provide an SDK flag so they can opt into sync validate, but default to async.
Priya Rao (DevEx): I'll draft SDK change: new request param validate_schema: ['strict','async','none'] and header x-redwood-validate. Put warning about possible malformed structured output if async/none. Also add examples showing x-redwood-skip-validate: true.
Maria Gomez (SRE): After canary, ACME-like customers in canary group saw p99 drop to ~800ms. I'll pin Northgate back to router-v1 to buy time while we implement code fix.
Alex Chen (Support): Noted customer happy with temporary fix; asked for timeline for permanent fix + changelog. Samir, estimate for code change to move validation off critical path?
Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): Hotfix timeline: 1) Flip to async validate permanently (config) ~30-45m with rollout. 2) Code change to move validation post-tool and add validation worker pool: ~3-5 days dev+test+staging. Will cut a PR today (link to follow).
JenkinsBot: ROLLBACK: routing rule applied, Northgate pinned to router-v1 at 07:36 UTC
Maria Gomez (SRE): Action items:
- Pin impacted customers (Maria)
- Flip ASYNC_VALIDATE to true cluster-wide after verification (Maria/Samir)
- PR to move validation off-path (Samir)
- SDK flag and docs (Priya)
- Add a telemetry metric: 'schema_validation_latency' histogram and 'router_tool_router_overhead' derived metric (Alex)
Alex Chen (Support): Customer acceptance: they confirmed p99 improved after pin and canary; asked to be updated when async becomes default. They've accepted temporary workaround.
Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/router/pulls/1298 - implements off-path validation and adds a validation worker pool. Benchmark: off-path reduces avg router CPU by ~30% and cuts validation tail by ~120-160ms for multi-tool flows.
Priya Rao (DevEx): Drafted support note with examples and trade-offs. Will add to status page: note about schema validation mode and impacts on latency.
OpsBot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2031 - p99 regression mitigated by routing pin + async canary
Alex Chen (Support): Tracking tickets: SUP-4521, ENG-9042. Will prepare a short postmortem once fix is deployed.
Maria Gomez (SRE): Monitoring shows steady state after canary roll; will keep watch for next 24h.
Alex Chen (Support): Everyone ack?
Samir Patel (Eng Runtime): ack
Priya Rao (DevEx): ack
Maria Gomez (SRE): ack
OpsBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-2031 - mitigated; follow-ups scheduled
Alex Chen (Support): Closing thread. Follow-ups in tickets and PRs. Thanks all.
